review_notes: Read the whole target file, the definitions of initialInverseChart/initialForwardChart and their only simp lemmas (the `_zero` ones), and grepped for how the nonzero branch is unfolded across the repo. The unfolding `rw [initialInverseChart, dite_eq_right hs]` appears in many files. The first lemma and the `inverse_uniform_bound` theorem involve only arithmetic and have no simp-interface issues. I could not run Lean, so the proposed lemma is untested. I did not check how the other unfolding sites would behave after the change.

findings.problem: `initialInverseChart` has a simp lemma only for the `t = 0` branch (`initialInverseChart_zero`). The nonzero branch has no lemma, so each proof unfolds the definition and then rewrites with `dite_eq_right hs`. The same two-step idiom appears in InitialInverseChart.lean (initialInverseChart_differentiableOn, initialInverseChart_displacement), InitialChartIdentities.lean, InitialChartNormalization.lean, SlitBoundaryTip.lean, FutureSlitDomain.lean, InitialDrivingTip.lean, InitialInverseLimitAt.lean, InitialCapacityContinuity.lean, DrivingEndpointUniqueness.lean and more. The zero case has a canonical simp rewrite and the nonzero case does not, so the interface is incomplete and every use exposes the raw `dite`. The `initialForwardChart` and `initialCapacity` definitions have the same gap.
findings.proposed_change: In InitialInverseChart.lean, next to `initialInverseChart_zero`, add a lemma `initialInverseChart_of_ne_zero (hs : s ≠ 0) : initialInverseChart p hi h0 hH s = (initialSlitChart p hi h0 hH s hs).inverse`, proved by `dif_neg hs`, and mark it `@[simp]`. Add analogous lemmas for `initialForwardChart` and `initialCapacity`. Then line 62 becomes `rw [initialInverseChart_of_ne_zero hs]` (or `simp only [...]`). The `s = 0` branch can then close with `simp` instead of `subst s; rw …; change …; linarith`.
findings.benefit: Gives the definition a complete simp interface: both branches have named rewrite rules, so the `dite` stays hidden. Call sites become shorter and no longer depend on the definition's `if ht : t=0` shape. The `hs` hypothesis is the side condition, so the rule applies only when it should.
